incident-bot: [ALERT] high error-rate on inference-prod (5xx spike) :rotating_light: 

Sara (SRE): acked. investigating. paging on-call. please avoid mass replies in channel unless critical. :eyes: 

Michael (Support): pinged on-call (michael-oncall). pulling logs now — any customer-facing impact yet?

Sara (SRE): early triage: increased 503s coming from batch-svc during amplification window. symptoms: timeouts to runtime, queue growth. possible autoscaler thrash. no confirmed data loss.

Priya (Support Lead): Michael, please use the short customer macro below for any inbound tickets while we investigate. Keep replies minimal and set expectation for next update in 30m.

Michael (Support): copying macro into thread for agents to reuse (Zendesk/Intercom):

```
Macro: Incident - Inference Errors (short)
Subject: We're investigating increased errors affecting model responses
Body: Hi {{customer_first_name}},
Thanks for the report — our team is aware of an issue causing intermittent errors for some inference requests. We're actively investigating and will share an update within 30 minutes. If you have request IDs or timestamps, please include them and we'll prioritize those.
Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your service.
— Redwood Support
```

Eli (AE): can we add a one-liner about retry guidance? customers asking whether to retry client-side.

Sara (SRE): yes — add this line to the macro: "Client retries with exponential backoff (2xx ms jitter) are safe; avoid immediate tight loops."

Michael (Support): also adding a slightly more technical snippet for customers who are seeing 503s:

```
Suggested client-side retry snippet (node):
const wait = ms => new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms));
async function callWithRetry(fn, attempts=3) {
  for (let i=0;i<attempts;i++) {
    try { return await fn(); } catch (e) {
      const backoff = Math.pow(2, i) * 100 + Math.floor(Math.random()*100);
      await wait(backoff);
    }
  }
  throw new Error('failed after retries');
}
```

Priya (Support Lead): good. also paste the internal troubleshooting checklist (agents) — minimal steps first, escalate to SRE if step 4 fails.

Michael (Support): internal checklist (copy/paste friendly):
1) Collect customer request IDs, timestamps, region, model name.
2) Run quick health checks: 
   - API gateway: `curl -sS https://api.redwood.example/health` 
   - Runtime ping: `curl -sS https://runtime-usw2.internal/_health`
3) Check queue/backlog (SRE dashboard or Redis): look for >500 queued items -> escalate.
4) If you see 5xx spike in logs, paste top 5 log samples into the ticket.
5) If step 3 or 4 true -> escalate to oncall SRE with subject: "ESCALATE: inference-prod 5xx spike - <ticket#>" and include collected data.

Sara (SRE): for SREs — quick triage commands:
```
# show pod restart and CPU thundering
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep batch-svc
kubectl logs deploy/batch-svc --since=10m | tail -n 200
# check redis queue length (prod-red-queue)
redis-cli -h prod-redis info keyspace | grep red-queue
```
If autoscaler thrash suspected: `kubectl describe hpa batch-svc -n inference`

incident-bot: New oncall handoff note: @michael please include this H/O checklist when you hand off in 30m.

Michael (Support): Handoff template (outgoing -> incoming oncall):
- Summary: brief one-line (what happened)
- Current state: mitigations applied, whether traffic rerouted, working-around steps
- Open customer tickets: list ticket IDs with priority and any impacted customers
- Next steps: what to monitor and known flakiness items
- Links: dashboards, runbooks, incident channel link

Priya (Support Lead): status page guidance (internal): keep first status brief and non-technical. example: "Partial service disruption: some inference requests may fail or be delayed. Our engineers are investigating." Save deeper technical analysis for later updates.

Sara (SRE): status page suggested update (technical note for the postmortem): 
"Cause: runtime autoscaler attempted scale-down during high-traffic amplification window, causing repeated cold starts and timeouts. Mitigation: pinned minimum replicas, temporarily disabled aggressive scale-to-zero behavior. Followup: adjust scaling policies and add circuit-breaker on batch queue depth."

Michael (Support): ETA/updates cadence: post initial customer-facing reply within 15 minutes, internal update every 30 minutes in thread, status page update within 30 minutes. If customer asks for SLA credits, route to Priya/CS.

Eli (AE): If a customer requests a private postmortem, what's the ask flow?

Priya (Support Lead): escalate to CS (Priya) -> SRE PM for postmortem. Include timeline, impact, and committed remediation. We'll follow enterprise disclosure policy.

Michael (Support): quick note for agents: save all canned responses you use as ticket macros; prefix with INCIDENT-yyyy-mm-dd so we can audit later.

Sara (SRE): ongoing: I'm keeping autoscaler pinned for now. I'll post updates once we see error-rate drop below threshold. please escalate any high-priority customers immediately.

incident-bot: incident channel pinned message updated: https://redwoodincidents.example/1845012345

Michael (Support): thanks team — using macros now. will post customer updates and handoff to @support-next at 1845012480.

Priya (Support Lead): documented — thanks everyone.
